extracted.intended_audience: administrative law scholars, policymakers, agency designers, and regulatory practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and design principles for structuring administrative processes (especially notice-and-comment and agency organization) to institutionalize agonistic democratic virtues: pluralistic participation, visible conflict, dispersed accountability, and avenues for contestation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairly balanced advisory committees / reserved seats for affected groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal advisory committees should be 'fairly balanced in terms of the view represented' (FACA) and may reserve seats for representatives of specific groups to ensure underrepresented perspectives are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include patient representatives on FDA advisory committees, representatives of Indian tribes on BLM resource advisory councils, and councils constituted specifically to advance particular perspectives (e.g., National Environmental Justice Advisory Council). The intent is to contribute underrepresented perspectives to decision making by designating membership slots for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted outreach to stakeholder communities during notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should 'conduct targeted outreach to important stakeholder communities' to ensure important perspectives are likely to be heard during the comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACUS has recommended building on existing agency experiments. Techniques include purposive identification of participants, focus groups to 'gauge participants’ reactions to information, ideas, messages, or proposals,' and other supplemental engagement methods to surface perspectives that might not appear in mass commenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematize outreach and solicitation so agencies confront implications when critical perspectives are absent
rubrics_metrics.description: Outreach must be institutionalized so agencies are forced to grapple with the implications of proposals 'even when no one voices critical perspectives.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From an agonistic standpoint, such systematized solicitation prevents invisible harms from being ignored and ensures agencies must confront dissent as a regular feature of policymaking rather than an occasional anomaly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not seek to manufacture consensus; make conflict visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies adopting an agonistic standpoint should reject approaches that 'seek to forge consensus' and should avoid trying to convince participants 'that the agency’s proposal is good for everyone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, agencies should 'forthrightly acknowledge that the proposal may not be good for everyone and ensure that all are forced to confront that fact and accept the consequences,' while providing 'ample opportunities to force revisitation of that temporary settlement.' Honest outreach that exposes disagreement is preferred to consensus-forging deliberation (which may fail or suppress conflict).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatten bureaucratic hierarchy / disperse accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer dispersal of authority and multiple lines of accountability over concentrating control in the presidency; 'flattening the administrative state—not hierarchizing it—is the best way to preserve [messiness] and give conflict a chance to thrive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entails permitting Congress to vest significant authority in officers accountable to constituencies beyond the President, and resisting doctrines and institutional reforms (e.g., removability and appointments rules) that reify a singular presidential accountability model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiply institutional sites of contestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain multiple, multi-directional sites of authority and accountability (between agencies, between agencies and branches, and between agencies and society) to enhance democratic mobilization and meaningful politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text cites interagency disputes (e.g., FCC vs FAA on 5G) as examples where overlapping authority produced public attention and genuine politics. Agonistic design values the friction that such overlaps create.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable Congress to experiment with diversifying constituencies and adversarial checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress should be allowed (and encouraged) to design institutions that diversify the constituencies to which agency officials answer and to subject agency decision making to adversarial checks at multiple levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congress has already used creative techniques to insulate some agencies from presidential control; the argument is for permitting further experimentation under the Necessary and Proper Clause with decentered accountability mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and expand private-citizen enforcement mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Private-citizen enforcement (citizen suits) should be preserved or expanded because it empowers individuals to bring litigation and acts as a lever that forces public decision making back into democratic politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though often criticized as 'meddlesome,' from an agonistic perspective citizen suits are valuable levers of accountability. Caution: some forms (e.g., 'bounty hunter' enforcement in rights-suppressing laws) are distinct and problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decenter the presidency as the sole lodestar of administrative accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the 'presidential control model' that ties democratic accountability exclusively to presidential elections; embrace decentered forms of accountability that include non-hierarchical organizational structures and practices keeping agencies attuned to affected publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument is that presidential centralization simplifies politics to election moments and narrows the scope of legitimate contestation; agonism sees distributed accountability as more democratically robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be pragmatic: moderate agonistic features where other values outweigh them
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply agonistic institutionalization contextually; do not maximize agonism in every setting because other values (expertise, efficiency, stability) sometimes justify moderating agonistic mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author emphasizes a pragmatic orientation toward democracy and recognizes real tradeoffs—agonistic reforms should be sensitive to context and not pursued dogmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use agonism to provide procedural legitimacy and manage citizen frustration
rubrics_metrics.description: Agonism can function as a device of procedural justice by acknowledging burdens placed on citizens and offering meaningful opportunities for redress, thereby increasing perceptions of legitimacy even when outcomes are disliked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telling dissidents that their frustration is legitimate and ensuring 'substantial opportunities to pursue redress' can 'cool the mark out' and contribute to willingness to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept and design for greater policy friction and oscillation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that agonistic institutionalization may increase friction in policymaking—making significant, lasting policy changes harder and policy more oscillatory—and treat that as an acceptable or intended feature to recalibrate democratic expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because agonism reflects true preference diversity, enduring policy may be scarce; this can reduce incentives for zero-sum politics by making 'wins' ephemeral and encouraging constructive engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand conflict scope to enable marginalized groups to challenge entrenched interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Use agonistic mechanisms to expand the sites and scope of political conflict so marginalized constituencies have 'ample opportunities' to counter entrenched or favored interests within administrative politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanding contestation both challenges narratives that the administrative state persistently favors entrenched interests and may alter underlying power dynamics by enabling counter-mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat civil-servant dissent and disobedience as a legitimate agonistic problem to resolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that civil servants will often disagree with political appointees or presidential commands and that resolving the ethical and legal questions around civil-servant disobedience is an aspect of agonistic administrative design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The civil service's persistence across administrations makes conflict with political directives inevitable; agonistic theory frames such conflicts as intrinsic democratic features to be managed rather than pathologies to be suppressed.
